note: Household debt excluding accruals was SEK 5,530.49 billion in Q1 2026 according to SCB financial accounts. The 2026 Spring Fiscal Policy Bill states that mortgages account for more than 80 % of household debt. The visual deliberately omits the debt-to-income ratio because Statistics Sweden corrected the disposable-income denominator on 24 June 2026 and will update that series on 17 September 2026. Regulation timeline: mortgage cap 85 % (2010), amortisation requirement (2016), enhanced requirement (2018), and April 2026 changes. For a new purchase the cap is 90 %; later top-up loans are capped at 80 %. The enhanced income-based requirement is removed while the base requirement remains up to 2 %/yr depending on loan-to-value.
